claims.explanation: Simvastatin's selective killing likely reflects dependence on the mevalonate/cholesterol-biosynthesis pathway and on the geranylgeranyl-pyrophosphate-dependent prenylation of small GTPases, so lines with high HMGCR-pathway activity or strong reliance on prenylation-dependent survival signaling (e.g., RAS/RAF/PI3K-driven) are most sensitive, while lines with low pathway flux or compensatory survival signaling are protected. The virtual-cell signature (HMGCR upregulation, cell-cycle/mitotic gene suppression, and similarity to other statins) supports on-target HMGCR inhibition with downstream effects on proliferation and survival.

features.basis: on-target dependence; statin-class mechanism and virtual-cell HMGCR upregulation
KRAS-driven lines require geranylgeranylation for survival, enhancing statin sensitivity
RAS-family prenylation dependence sensitizes to HMGCR inhibition
MAPK-driven melanomas/colorectal lines are enriched among sensitive lines
PI3K/AKT activation may increase dependence on mevalonate-derived survival signals
PI3K-pathway activation observed in several sensitive lines
RAS-pathway activation via NF1 loss in multiple sensitive lines
TP53-mutant lines are common in both extremes, so p53 loss alone is not sufficient and may blunt statin-induced apoptosis
EGFR-mutant lung lines appear among least-affected lines, suggesting EGFR signaling compensates for statin stress
MEK activation in a least-affected line suggests MAPK-driven survival can offset statin effects
SF3B1-mutant lines appear in both extremes but enriched among least-affected, suggesting spliceosome-linked resistance
WNT/beta-catenin activation in several least-affected lines may support statin-resistant survival
